title: Genghis Khan: Madman or Genius?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant examine Genghis Khan, the 13th-century Mongol leader, weighing his reputation as a revered military mastermind against his role as a conqueror responsible for enormous loss of life. They cover his obscure childhood (born Temujin, kidnapping-based tribal society, family exile after his father's poisoning), his rise through alliances and talent-spotting, his unification of the Mongol tribes and adoption of the Genghis Khan title in 1206, the Mongol cavalry and tactics that made them effective, the campaigns against the Tangut, Jin and Khwarazmian empires, his death and unknown burial place, his legacy (trade, the yam postal system, descendants), how Mongolia reveres him after Soviet suppression, and a Mongol propaganda manuscript. The episode closes with listener mail about a Brazilian billionaire's planned Bentley burial stunt meant to promote organ donation.

entities.name: The Brutal Brilliance of Genghis Khan

segments.title: Opening banter and Phoenix show news
segments.summary: Josh announces the Phoenix show moving to the Orpheum Theater, then the hosts introduce the Genghis Khan topic and the pronunciation and name debate.

segments.title: Statue, reputation, and scale of conquest
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the giant equestrian statue in Mongolia, the divided historical views of Genghis Khan, the estimated deaths of about 35 million people, and the size of his empire compared with the Roman Empire.

segments.title: Mongol world context and birth of Temujin
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Mongols' rapid rise with the world at the time and cover the uncertain birth around 1162 near the Onon River, plus Temujin's position among his brothers.

segments.title: Kidnapping customs and Yesugei's family
segments.summary: They discuss the lawless tribal world of the steppe, the practice of kidnapping wives, and how Temujin's father Yesugei took his mother Hoelun. Yesugei was poisoned when Temujin was nine, and the family was cast out.

segments.title: Sources and Temujin's charisma
segments.summary: The hosts cover the Secret History of the Mongols as the main primary source, then describe Temujin's charisma and early stories of gaining allies and recruiting talent, including the enemy archer later named Jebe.

segments.title: Unifying the tribes and the title Genghis Khan
segments.summary: Temujin builds his following through alliances and conquests, accepts surrender from those who did not resist, and is proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206 at a great assembly. The tribes renounce their rivalries and identify as Mongols.

segments.title: Mongol military strength and tactics
segments.summary: The hosts explain Mongol advantages: horsemanship, archery, cavalry without infantry, light armor, the hooked lance, scouting and planning, the decimal unit structure, and a surrender-or-die policy that discouraged resistance.

segments.title: Siege tactics and cat and bird story
segments.summary: They discuss Genghis Khan's dislike of walled cities, the use of catapults and diseased animals, the story of cats and birds set on fire, and the term apocalypse.

segments.title: Campaigns against China, Central Asia, and death
segments.summary: The hosts cover the campaigns against the Tangut, Jin and Khwarazmian empires, the estimated China death toll, the shift to administration, and Genghis Khan's death around 1227 with unknown burial. Mongol legacy includes trade, noodles, tea, and the yam postal system.

segments.title: Legacy debate, Mongolian reverence, and propaganda
segments.summary: The hosts discuss modern Mongolian reverence after Soviet suppression, the author's argument that Mongol cruelty was typical for the era, Hollywood portrayals, and Mongol illustrated propaganda histories.
